data.hypothesis: The previously measured four-lane candidate was correct, with a reported mean of 0.1917555 s versus 0.5634215 s for the baseline, but the available observations do not provide an explicit per-thread breakdown. This eight-lane scalar interleave tests whether more independent recurrence chains hide dependency latency; additional active-lane checks, register pressure, and differing escape lengths could instead erase any benefit.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use this as motivation for a width comparison, not as proof that wider interleaving improves one-thread throughput; the available measurements do not separate thread budgets.

memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this eight-lane variant against the baseline at one thread and report the four-core-budget result separately.
